I stayed at this hostel for about 1.5 months and had already paid for my stay through June 21. On June 10, I was told to leave before the end of my paid period. From my perspective, it seemed that new guests who were willing to pay more were being prioritized, and I do not think it was fair to ask a paying guest to leave early.

What was most disappointing was that I was not offered a satisfactory solution regarding the unused portion of my payment. This created a stressful situation and left me scrambling to find alternative accommodation on short notice.

The facilities were also lacking. During my stay, there was often no toilet paper provided, which is a basic necessity that guests should not have to worry about.

My experience left me feeling that existing guests were not treated fairly or professionally. I would advise future guests to make sure they clearly understand the hostel’s policies regarding long-term stays, refunds, and early termination before booking.

featured_reviews.name: Suman Das
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently stayed at Happinest Hostel in Bandra, Mumbai, and it was a fantastic experience overall. The location is one of the best features – it's just 600-700 meters from Bandra Railway Station, making it super convenient for commuting, exploring the trendy Bandra area, or catching trains to other parts of the city.

The rooms are comfortable, with excellent room service keeping everything tidy. The washrooms and toilets are well-maintained and clean, which is a big plus for a hostel stay. What I loved most is the self-catering kitchen setup: you can easily prepare quick breakfasts or light meals like toast, omelettes, or simple dishes. There's a fridge for storing your food, and all the necessary dishes and utensils are provided for cooking and eating – it really feels like a home away from home.

Other amenities are thoughtful too: a washing machine is available (though chargeable), a dedicated smoking area where you can relax and chill with friends, and a common TV area with free access to Netflix, YouTube, and more for unwinding. Towels and locks are available for rent if needed.
The owner is friendly and approachable, and they even offer monthly stays with direct negotiation for better rates – perfect for longer-term visitors.

There are some reasonable rules in place, like no cooking or noise in the kitchen area after 11 AM (to avoid disturbing others sleeping nearby), no smoking area access after 1 AM, restrictions on the TV area late at night (around 2:30-4 AM), and no gathering at the entrance gate after 1 AM. These rules are genuinely fair and help maintain a peaceful environment for everyone – no complaints there!

Overall, This Hostel offers great value with its prime location, practical facilities, and considerate management. It's ideal for solo travelers, backpackers, or anyone looking for a comfortable, no-fuss stay in Mumbai. I thoroughly enjoyed my time here and would definitely return!

Special thanks to Mr. Barun.(Receptionist/Caretaker also)
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
Dear Suman,

Wow, we're beaming with joy reading your kind words about HappiNest Hostel!
We're thrilled you found our little Bandra haven comfortable and convenient – that's exactly what we aim for.

A big shoutout to Mr. Barun and the entire team for keeping things running smoothly. Your feedback fuels our fire to keep improving!

Hope to welcome you back soon for another cozy stay. Until next time, Mumbai awaits! 🌟

featured_reviews.name: gvr
featured_reviews.review_text:
I stayed at this hostel for four days in April. It’s an acceptable place for short stays, but I wouldn’t recommend it for medium or long-term stays.
The room was quite small, the walls are made of plaster, and noise travels easily. The door was also very noisy when opening and closing, which was a bit annoying.
I had an issue with the laundry service: I started using the washing machine and was later told the cost was 300 rupees, even though a sign there said 200. They also told me the service was handled by staff, but in practice, the clothes were left unattended for quite a while, and I ended up having to take care of hanging and collecting them myself.
On the positive side, the accommodation has air conditioning, which is a plus. However, the person in charge, Suraj, sleeps in the common area and does not speak English, which can be a significant drawback in an international city like Mumbai.
Overall, it’s a functional place for a short stay, but there are several aspects that could be improved.
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
Thanks for spending four days with us and for the detailed feedback. We really appreciate the honesty - it helps us get better.
HappiNest is a 100+ year-old heritage property, so things like plaster walls, smaller rooms, and creaky wooden doors come with the charm and the challenges. We’re adding door dampeners and clearer quiet hours to help with the sound.
You’re right about the laundry mix-up. We upgraded to a new, bigger machine and the rate is now ₹300, but we forgot to update the old ₹200 poster. Sorry for that confusion and the service gap - we’ve fixed the sign and are retraining the team so the process is clear.
Noted on Suraj too. He’s part of our night support team and stays in the common area for guest safety. We’re rostering more English-speaking staff on shift to make communication easier for international guests.
Glad the AC helped during your April stay. We know we’ve got work to do, especially for longer stays.
Thanks again for helping us preserve this old Bandra home while improving the experience.

featured_reviews.review_text: Absolutely loved my stay at HappiNest! The staff were friendly and helpful, the rooms and specially washrooms were clean and comfortable and the location was perfect in the centre of Bandra. Hygiene is taken care meticulously in shared spaces and well-equipped kitchen is perfect for preparing light meals, making it ideal for longer stays. Overall , it's a most comfortable place to relax and unwind.

featured_reviews.name: Vimal Dubey
featured_reviews.review_text:
The biggest issue is the deposit refund. The owner does not return the full deposit and creates unnecessary problems during the process. In my case, only around 60% of the deposit was returned, and the remaining amount was deducted without any clear or valid explanation. Charges were applied arbitrarily, which felt unfair.

I had to call more than 30 times just to get updates on my deposit, and many times the owner did not even pick up the calls. This made the whole process very frustrating and unprofessional.

Major suggestion: do not leave the PG until your full deposit is returned, as it becomes very difficult to recover the remaining amount later.

The PG had basic amenities and was manageable for staying, but there were several issues. Initially, there were problems with filtered water and the AC, which caused inconvenience. Although the owner fixed these after complaints, it took time and effort to get them resolved. Cleaning was done daily, which is a positive point, but there were still cockroaches in the kitchen, which was not hygienic.

The management is supportive, safety is well taken care of, and the overall vibe stays calm and respectful. People who live here understand the comfort, discipline, and convenience it offers. As for the haters , when a place does things right, noise is inevitable. Quality doesn’t argue, it simply exists. Those who know, know. ✨💯
